SourceString: A different line of work begins today.
The bees have settled in nicely. Judging by the buzzing, they approve.
A new member has joined your family.
Their application for office has been received. Serving the people is a noble ambition. Serving the family is a much more practical one.
Your candidacy has been received. May the best candidate win the seat!
During the hunt you spot movement in the brush and shout “Boar!”\nSpears rise, riders scatter. A rabbit hops out. The laughter lasts longer than the hunt.
Sir Ulrich falls injured before the next tilt. The challenger still waits in the lists. You mount and ride out to face him, showing your courage.
Sir Ulrich rides into the competition when his armor suddenly comes loose, plates clattering before the crowd. The mistake is yours.
Raiders enter the camp at night. You stop the first attacker before he reaches the tents. The knights wake and the fight begins. If not for you, they would be dead! They recognize your worth.
You repeat a rumor you heard at the table. The hall grows quiet. By morning, the court knows you cannot keep a secret.
A secret is spoken just loudly enough for you to hear. Others later try to coax it from you. You keep it. Perhaps you belong among them after all.
Countess Báthory raises a toast in honor of her recently departed husband. You speak at the wrong moment. All eyes turn to you.
Two knights dispute who deserves credit for a victory. You ask which one would have won alone. Neither answers. The hall decides the glory belongs to both.
During Colonel Sandersdorf's visit, your hand slips and wine stains his pristine clothes. A costly mistake.
Just before the toast, you catch the scent of poison in the cup. These nobles owe you their lives. You earn their recognition.
No one can deny that a noble's greatest virtue is wealth.

Some of these fellows would lose a battle against the rats from Tom's bakery — but you get what you pay for.
As the decent person you are, it is only natural not to want to be associated with those men. Judging by the look of them, they are bound to cause trouble.
If every robber were like those, the town would not last long.
What an inspiring tale!

Guaranteed to bring you down.

There she is! You place her in a basket, and the swarm follows. Time to start your own hive!
You declare an heir. May they honor the family name or die trying!
The quarter looks better for your trouble. A few less ruins, a little less filth, and considerably more dignity.
There now. Even the spiders must move out.
You've poisoned a buch of hardworking bees. \nThey were just trying to make honey.
What Did The Bees Ever Do to You?

Bee-trayal!
Soft, golden, and pleasantly fragrant. A fine harvest of beeswax!

Your beloved was deeply offended by the gift. Did you mean to suggest they were as wild and ill-tempered as a bear?
After some discussion about where to keep the bear, they were thrilled by the grand gesture.
Unfortunately, your beloved has never been able to stomach dairy. They promptly rolled the enormous cheese wheel down a hill and watched it disappear into the distance.
Your beloved was delighted! They fetched a small hammer and carefully tapped the cheese wheel, listening for imperfections before declaring it a masterpiece.
The cloak itself drew praise. Your family crest did not. They asked whether the embroidery could be removed without damaging the fabric.
The cloak has barely left your beloved's shoulders since you gave it to them. Better yet, they make no effort to hide your family crest.
The bouquet looked lovely, until a bee emerged from the blossoms and stung your beloved on the nose. The flowers received a rather chilly welcome.
At your next meeting, you notice one of your flowers tucked into your beloved's hair. They catch you looking and smile.
The golden bathtub wouldn't fit through the doorway. After two hours of arguing with the deliverymen, your beloved politely declined your suggestion to remove the wall.
A bath of warm rosewater was ordered at once. Your beloved has already declared that they will never set foot in an ordinary bathtub again.
Their eyes went straight to the jewels. Then came the question: \n\"Do you think my hair looks untidy?\" \nThe conversation never quite recovered.
Your beloved has begun styling their hair twice a day, just for an excuse to use their beautiful new hairbrush.
The horse was admired from the far side of the courtyard. Apparently, your beloved is terrified of riding and would prefer that the animal remain at a very respectable distance.
Before the stablehand could finish praising the horse's pedigree, your beloved was already in the saddle. An invitation for you to join them on a ride soon followed.
Your beloved thought you were proposing marriage and began explaining, very gently, why they weren't ready.
Your beloved cried out “Yes!” the moment they saw the rings. When you gently explained that you weren't proposing, they blushed with embarrassment, then asked you not to forget their answer.
Your beloved complimented your beautiful handwriting. Unfortunately, they had remarkably little to say about the poetry itself.
Your beloved thanked you for the beautiful poem and promised to write something equally heartfelt in return.
Your beloved stared at the imaginary children in silence. After an uncomfortable pause, they complimented the frame.
Your beloved was thrilled! They recognized every child in the portrait, though they were rather upset that you had forgotten to include little Margaret.
The craftsmanship is exquisite, but your beloved objects to one detail: the tapestry depicts them swooning into your arms. They insist they did no such thing.
The tapestry has been given a place of honor, and your beloved has spent the afternoon showing it to every visitor. The story of your first date has now been told at least a dozen times.

The courtship has begun. Hearts are not won without effort: {A_SWETAL_C}sweet-talk{##} your chosen one and {A_SENGIF_C}send gifts{##} to prove your devotion, as well as your pecuniary means. But mind the competition: some suitors will try to outdo and even undermine your efforts.
The Heart's Impatience
Your courtship has ended — hopefully on amicable terms.
A catastrophe has been averted! You've convinced your relative to end their courtship before it could turn into another unfortunate affair in Verona.
You must truly hate this person. The curse is cast.
A needle pricks your spine. Sorcery! Someone must have cursed you!
A Costly Victory
The hive is gone. The bees fought back to the end — a kind of courage you could never claim.
A Petty Victory
You took your grievance out on thousands of harmless bees. Proud of yourself?
Someone destroyed your hive
You find the hive {buildingname} ruined and the colony dying. One last bee crawls toward you, wings trembling, before going still in your hand.
The master was dismissed with a harsh reprimand and a small bag of coin. You are now in charge of the building again, so all mistakes are your own.
Your challenge has been sent. Steel yourself — the duel awaits if they accept.
The smoke clears, and the familiar buzzing is gone. The hive stands empty now.
The bees are fed, the buzzing is lively again, and the colony seems much happier for it.
Watching family follow in your footsteps has a certain satisfaction to it. With their place in the guild secured, they can now serve as {B_OCC_MGR_C}master{##} of one of your businesses.
But some of the guards were less pleased, worried you might be there to take their post.
And you even made a few friends over a story about the time you supposedly faced three armed men at once. The details changed slightly with every telling, but no one seemed to notice.
Unfortunately, the work was every bit as dangerous as it looked.
Some light fingers stay in their pockets thanks to you.
This one seems a proper jester. Best not be seen keeping company with their kind.
They do not seem like a bad sort. At least everyone laughed.
A guard volunteer claims they once saw a goose the size of a mountain. Either a liar or a remarkable storyteller.
tbd
Your cart is guarded. Those who attack will have to fight for it.
Everyone is talking about it.\nThe citizens have made up their minds — either feeling sympathy for its subject or laughing at their expense.
Laughter circles the Town Hall today but it slips away whenever you approach. A lampoon says you laugh at your own jokes before anyone can. How embarrassing!
Still, too much time spent shoulder to shoulder can give working folk ideas about their importance.
With you pacing the workshop, distractions quickly disappear and production improves.
The physician is not entirely sure what you have, but they are very interested in it.
The physician finds something in a place one tends to forget to check. A remedy is applied. Eye contact is not maintained.
Praise be to the heavens! The Lord hears your prayer.
Someone among the town servants takes a special interest in you.
Today you encounter someone serving the town. They leave quite an impression.
The physician gives you a bubbling concoction — “detox,” she says. It tastes awful, but it works.
Coin in your purse. What follows is no longer your concern.
Your letter of support and accompanying funds have been delivered.
Missed!
The cannon roared, the shot flew… and somehow, nothing was hit.
Direct Hit!
The shot found its mark. The following places were damaged:
A Waste of Dung
A spectacular launch, followed by absolutely no one getting covered in dung.
A Foul Hit!
The dung landed with disgusting accuracy. The following places will be difficult to approach for a while:
A Fiery Miss
A flash, a roar, and nothing to burn.
Up in Flames!
Fire caught fast. The following places are alight:
Carefully done. Their courtship shows its first cracks.
Doubt has been {A_SMEREP_C}planted{##} in your love interest's mind. Trust, once shaken, is slow to return.
The informants are grateful for your work — but a commoner may have spotted you snooping around.
Someone {A_SNI_C}reports{##} what happens in town to the informants. A necessary evil, or a traitor to the people?
A day at the inn, well spent. Tomorrow, a visit to the church should settle things.
Crime is down and the streets are safer. Yet somehow, people are complaining that the guards are becoming a bigger nuisance than the thieves. There is no pleasing some people.
The {O_COL_C}Colonel{##} ordered a {A_SUPCRI_C}crackdown on crime{##}, and now there are guards everywhere. The quarter is safer, sure, but good luck getting home without having your purse searched.
Crime is down. Things are staying where people left them.
The {O_FENMAS_C}Fencing Master{##} {A_SUPCRIW_C}stepped up the patrols{##}, and trouble in the quarter has quieted down. Nothing dramatic, just fewer reasons to clutch your purse on the way home.
Some tricks of the trade are best learned from those who already know them.
A few fellow professionals were happy to see you.
But that lesson took more out of you than expected. Best let it settle before trying again.
It is always good to see your workers thrive!
Even when they do not want to.
Better yet when they are grateful.
But they are clearly spent, and no more learning will stick for a while.
A hard lesson, but bruises are often fine teachers.
All that wax on, wax off has left you thirsty for an {I_ENDPOT_C}Endurance Drink{##}.
Steady hands improve with practice, and practice rarely comes free.
tbd
A good bargain begins long before anyone reaches for the coin.
tbd
A well-placed word can do more than a raised fist.
tbd
Best learn the tricks before someone tries them on you.

We, the Alchemists' Guild, grant you license. See that your experiments yield more than smoke.
We entrust you with the dead. Keep order — silence is no excuse for neglect.
We, the Guards' Guild, accept your oath. Stand watch — and do not fail it.
We, the Innkeepers' Guild, grant you license. Keep the ale flowing — and the rumors with it.

We, the Joiners' Guild, grant you license. Build well — what you make will be relied upon.
We, the Moneylenders' Guild, grant you license. See that every coin returns — with interest.
We, the Perfumers' Guild, grant you license. Leave an impression worth remembering.
Your oath is heard. Speak — and ensure they listen.
You've proven yourself. Take the road — and what travels upon it.
We, the Smiths' Guild, grant you license. Let iron answer to your hand.
We, the Stone Masons' Guild, grant you license. Build something that endures.
We, the Tailors' Guild, grant you license. Shape what others will wear — and be judged by.
You're in. Stay unseen — and take what matters.
We, the Merchants' Guild, grant you license. Trade well — and profit better.
Your troupe is recognized. Hold their gaze — and earn their coin.
Your worker listened closely to the tavern talk. No crime to report — just a poor fellow being mocked for snoring loud enough to wake the whole street.
Loose tongues and strong drink did their work. Evidence of a crime has surfaced.
They were either more roguish than your rogues… or simply had nothing worth taking.
Your thieves return with heavier pockets.
You spot a pair of long fingers reaching for your purse — but you dodge just in time. Everything's still there.
Your pockets feel lighter. Damn pickpockets!
Your rogues took what they could — if anything — and sold it for your profit. They're on their way back, leaving the quarter more dangerous than before.
Some rogues tried to break in and steal from you.

It's good to have connections. Your friendship with {office} {charactername} earned you a Nobility Charter — no blood, no sweat, just the right handshakes.
You've spent more time pouring drinks and pretending to care than anyone should. But at least you've got a Nobility Charter to show for it.
You've kissed more feet and lied through your teeth to stay afloat in those murky waters. But now you've got a Nobility Charter.
You've nearly met your end more times than you can count, but hey, you survived. Now, you get a Nobility Charter to prove it.

Someone brushes against you at the Marketplace. You don't notice at the time.
As you finish your drink, you notice something strange at the bottom of the cup. A moment later, your skull feels like it's on fire.
You fell asleep during the vote. There was snoring. Possibly drool. Let's just say it won't help your chances in this election.
There is evidence linking you to a crime you didn't commit. Violating {law}, they say. Good luck proving it never happened.
There is evidence linking you to crimes you didn't commit. Breaking the {law1} and {law2} laws, they say. Good luck proving it never happened.
{ActorName} gives you a bone bracelet. It's a simple gift, but it feels meaningful.
{ActorName} wears a musk scent. You catch a hint of it.
{ActorName} sends you a poem. You appreciate the gesture.
{ActorName} uses {ItemName}. You are impressed!
Someone uses a Stink Bomb on your business {BuildingName}. \nLuckily, no worker thinks the smell is bad enough to quit.
Someone uses a Stink Bomb on your business {BuildingName}. \n{amount} workers quit due to the repugnant smell.
You trip over your own feet. Good job accepting that drink from... wait, who was that again?
You feel something sticky on your doorknob. Someone uses a Toad Slime on your residence {BuildingName}. \nLuckily, it has no effect on you.
You feel something sticky on your doorknob. Someone uses a Toad Slime on your residence {BuildingName}. \nYou contract {IllnessName}.
A pain comes from nowhere. Like a needle driven straight into your spine.

{Target2Name} claims to have received a letter from you and is furious about its contents. You have no idea what they are talking about.
The church receives a letter from Rome — sealed, official, and filled with grave accusations against {Target1Name} — someone you once trusted, but now you can't help but doubt.

Your audience bursts into laughter, their face turning bright red. They can barely catch their breath!
A tax collector walks into a tavern. The innkeeper asks, “What will you have?” The tax collector replies, “Half of whatever everyone else is having.”
A little snort of laughter escapes them. They try to hide it, but you heard it.
A young man hears that his beard is finally coming in. He immediately goes to wait by the front gate. His friend asks, “What if it comes through the back?”
They stare at you for a moment, apparently waiting for the funny part.
One of two identical twins died. When a man met the surviving brother, he asked, “Was it you who died, or your brother?”
Your joke has struck a nerve! Instead of laughing, they demand an apology.
A merchant complains, “The donkey you sold me has died!” The seller replies, “How strange! It never did that while I owned it.”
Your beloved was utterly enchanted by your serenade. They begged you to sing another song, and then another. You may have found your most devoted admirer!
Your beloved winced at a particularly unfortunate note, then gently suggested that some feelings are better expressed in words.
Your intellectual chemistry is undeniable. The hours flew by, and somewhere between philosophy and theology, a different kind of spark was ignited.
Your beloved admires your intelligence. Who knew all those years arguing with strangers at the tavern about whether the king was secretly a lizard would finally pay off in romance?
Your beloved has learned something valuable today: never ask you a question unless they have an entire afternoon to spare.
You crushed their arguments, dismantled their logic, and left them with no shred of dignity to defend. A glorious victory!
It turns out you and your beloved have quite a lot in common! How delightful to finally meet someone with such excellent taste.
You listened attentively, asked thoughtful questions, and even resisted the urge to talk about yourself. Your beloved was thoroughly charmed. Who knew shutting up could be so effective?
Halfway through your fascinating explanation, your beloved began to wonder whether being alone forever might actually be preferable.

Some people just don't appreciate honesty! Your beloved mentioned how much they enjoy listening to birds sing, so you explained that those stupid animals are just screaming about worms and territory. It's not music! It's a bunch of tiny landlords having an argument!
The cart now has an official parking spot!
The workers bid their four-legged colleague a fond farewell, complete with a few pats and a treat or two. The cart is now ready to be assigned to another building.
Your child has been baptized, and your spouse couldn't be happier that you kept their chosen name. A blessed day for the whole family!

Your spouse gave you a rather nasty look when you announced the child's new name before the visiting Priest. Thankfully, they had the decency not to make a scene while he was there. The moment he left, however, was another matter entirely.

“Another family! In another town! Can you imagine? And all they left us was this farewell letter!” you wail, waving the conveniently discovered note before a gathering of horrified onlookers.
